title: QPortfolio Portfolio Data
description: Root document for a QPortfolio portfolio-definition file (qp_file_type = "QPortfolio Data"). A portfolio data is the opportunities plus their input data, master data, attributes and the rules/constraints that the optimizer later solves. All opportunity names referenced anywhere in this file must match the names defined in input_data exactly (names are the unique identifier for an opportunity).

metadata.description: Document header. For a portfolio file qp_file_type must be "QPortfolio Data".

qp_file_type.description: Discriminator for the document type: "QPortfolio Data" for a portfolio data file, "QPortfolio Scenario Data" for a scenario file, "QPortfolio Model" for a model file and "QPortfolio Bundle" for a bundle manifest. Required.

qp_version.description: Version of the QPortfolio application that wrote this file, e.g. 4.6. Optional; when omitted the importer assumes the current version. A version newer than the importing application's is refused.

settings.description: Portfolio-level settings: the portfolio's name, the calculation calendar and the discounting and inflation rates. Optional.

start_date.description: The first time period of the portfolio, as a date-only value (e.g. "2026-01-01"). The first calculation period is determined by the time unit's granularity — a start date of 2019-12-31 with a Year time unit uses 2019 as the start year.

time_unit.description: The periodicity of the portfolio calculations. Must equal the portfolio's time unit unless the import allows a change. Allowed values: `Month` — Monthly time periods.; `Quarter` — Quarterly time periods.; `Year` — Yearly time periods..

input_time_period_count.description: Length of the longest opportunity series; re-derived on import.

selection_time_period_count.description: Number of periods considered in optimization (the Planning Horizon).

adjustment_policy.description: Discounting and inflation settings used by the Disc and Inf expression function families. Optional.

convention.description: When within each time period cash flows are assumed to occur for discounting. Allowed values: `StartOfPeriod` — All cash flows are collected at the start of the period; the first period is time zero and is not discounted.; `MidPeriod` — Cash flows are discounted at the mid-point of each period (year 1 over 0.5 periods, year 2 over 1.5, …), better reflecting flows distributed across a period.; `EndOfPeriod` — The entire cash flow of a period is assumed to arrive at its very end..

annual_discount_rate.description: Annual effective discount rate used by the Disc, CumSumDisc and TotalDisc functions, as a fraction (0.1 = 10% per year).

annual_inflation_rate.description: Annual effective inflation rate used by the Inf, CumSumInf and TotalInf functions, as a fraction.

discount_date.description: Optional date discounting is anchored to. Omit when the portfolio discounts from its start date.

input_data.description: Per-opportunity opportunity input data: the time-series and scalar metric values (split into weighted outcomes for EV and Monte Carlo) that characterise each opportunity.

opportunity_outcomes.description: The opportunities (or master-data sets) and their metric data. opportunity_name must be unique across the file.

items.description: One opportunity (or master-data set) together with its weighted outcomes.

opportunity_name.description: Unique name of the opportunity. Must match exactly everywhere this opportunity is referenced (constraints, dependencies, groups, selections). Unique within its namespace; a namespaced name is the namespace path and the name joined by "/", e.g. "North/Well 1", with a "/" inside a name written "\/".

outcomes.description: The weighted outcomes for this opportunity. A certain opportunity has a single outcome; an uncertain one is split into several weighted outcomes (e.g. P90/P50/P10) for Monte Carlo. The probability-weighted expected value is used in calculations, optimization and constraints.

items.description: A single weighted outcome of an opportunity and the metric values it carries.

outcome_name.description: Name of this outcome, e.g. "P90", "P50", "P10" or a single base case.

weight.description: Probability weight of this outcome within the opportunity. Weights across an opportunity's outcomes are normalised to form the expected value. Optional: when every outcome of the opportunity omits it, the outcomes are weighted equally; when only some omit it, those outcomes get weight 0.

metric_values.description: The metric values for this outcome. Opportunities need not all populate the same set of metrics. For missing input metrics, all values default to 0.

items.description: The value of one metric for one outcome, either as a per-period time series or as a single scalar.

metric_name.description: Name of the metric, e.g. "Capex-Drilling". Must match the model's metric name.

values.description: The metric values. When scalar is false/absent this is a time series indexed by time period (values[0] = period 0, values[1] = period 1, …). When scalar is true the single value (values[0]) applies regardless of period.

unit.description: Unit label for display, e.g. "$ MM", "bbl/d". Missing or null = the metric's unit; "" = no unit. A metric has one unit across every opportunity and outcome in this section.

scalar.description: When true, this metric is a single scalar (constant in time) rather than a per-period time series. Optional; defaults to false (time series). Must be the same for a metric across every opportunity and outcome in this section.

master_data.description: Master data: array inputs that are constant period-to-period but may differ across periods and across sets (e.g. price decks, FX, inflation, fiscal parameters). Matched to opportunities/scenarios via attributes. A default set with no attributes should exist. Each non-scalar series should hold at least selection_time_period_count + input_time_period_count - 1 values; any length imports. A set or metric here may not also appear in input_data, and a set may not appear in selection_constraints.

opportunity_outcomes.description: The opportunities (or master-data sets) and their metric data. opportunity_name must be unique across the file.

attributes.description: Attribute definitions and the per-opportunity characteristic values used to group, filter and match data (e.g. Country = Canada).

A set of attribute (category) names, e.g. ["Country", "Project Type"]. Optional. When an opportunity's characteristics omit any of these names, its value is treated as unset (null). The sole purpose of this set is to minimize explicit null characteristic entries for each opportunity.

items.description: The characteristic values assigned to one opportunity, plus its ordering/offset.

opportunity_name.description: Unique name of the opportunity these characteristics belong to.

order.description: Display/sort order of the opportunity within the portfolio. Optional; when omitted, the entry's position in opportunity_attributes sets its order.

is_order_global.description: When true, order is a manually assigned global position and is preserved as-is. Optional; defaults to false.

offset.description: Optional start-period offset applied to this opportunity's data (number of periods its series was shifted). This value defines base selection. A new opportunity starts at 0.

is_master_data.description: When true this row describes a master-data set rather than a selectable opportunity. Optional; defaults to false. When given it must match the section: true for a master_data set, false for an opportunity in input_data or selection_constraints.

characteristics.description: The attribute/value pairs assigned to this opportunity.

items.description: A single attribute/value pair, e.g. attribute = "Country", value = "Canada".

value.description: The characteristic value for this attribute. Null/absent means unset. A Date attribute's value is an Excel serial-date number as text, e.g. "45322" = 2024-01-31; a Numeric attribute's is a plain number as text.

outcome_dependency.description: Outcome dependencies: probabilistic correlations that reweight a dependent opportunity's outcomes based on the sampled outcome of an independent opportunity in each Monte Carlo trial. A rule family that belongs to versioned data, not to a scenario's selection rules.

dependencies.description: The outcome-dependency rules. At most one active (not disabled) rule per dependent_opportunity.

items.description: One outcome-dependency rule: how the dependent opportunity's outcome weights are reweighted given the independent opportunity's sampled outcome.

disabled.description: When true the rule is present but ignored. Optional; defaults to false.

independent_opportunity.description: Name of the independent opportunity whose sampled outcome drives the rule.

dependent_opportunity.description: Name of the dependent opportunity whose outcome weights are replaced.

target_cases.description: The mapping cases: for each set of sampled independent outcomes, the replacement outcome weights to apply to the dependent opportunity.

items.description: One case of an outcome dependency: when the independent opportunity samples any of the listed outcomes, apply the given dependent outcome weights.

independent_outcomes.description: The independent opportunity's outcome name(s) this case matches, e.g. ["P90"]. Use "*" to match all independent outcomes not listed explicitly; "*" must stand alone in its list. An outcome name may appear in only one case of a rule.

outcome_weights.description: The replacement weights to apply to the dependent opportunity's outcomes for this case.

items.description: A replacement weight for one (or more) of the dependent opportunity's outcomes.

dependent_outcomes.description: The dependent opportunity's outcome name(s) this weight applies to, e.g. ["P50"]. Use "*" to match all dependent outcomes not listed in this case; "*" must stand alone in its list. An outcome name may appear only once per case.

weight.description: The replacement probability weight to assign to those outcomes for this case.

selection_constraints.description: Selection constraints: per-opportunity bounds on how many times and when an opportunity may be selected by the optimizer. This belongs to selection rules, and may vary per scenario.

items.description: Selection limits scoped to one named opportunity.

opportunity_name.description: Unique name of the opportunity these limits apply to.

disabled.description: When true the constraint is present but ignored. Optional; defaults to false.

integer_only.description: When true the optimizer may only make whole (integer) selections of this unit — no partial/fractional selection.

interior_limit.description: Min Fraction: the minimum quantity that must be selected IF the unit is selected (it does not force selection). Applies per instance and only when non-integer selection is allowed; ignored when integer_only is true. Optional.

total_minimum.description: Minimum total selection summed across the entire span of eligible periods (aggregate, not per period). A positive value forces selection.

total_maximum.description: Maximum total selection summed across the entire span of eligible periods (aggregate, not per period). 0 forbids selection.

total_instances_minimum.description: Minimum number of instances (each in-period selection counts as one instance regardless of fractional size; 1.1 counts as two). A positive value forces selection. Optional.

total_instances_maximum.description: Maximum number of instances allowed. Optional.

time_period_minima.description: Per-period minimum selections, indexed by time period (element 0 = period 0). A positive entry forces selection in that period. May be empty (no per-period minima) or shorter than the horizon (unspecified periods are unbounded below). Entries past selection_time_period_count are stored but not used.

time_period_maxima.description: Per-period maximum selections, indexed by time period (element 0 = period 0). Caps selection in that period, and 0 forbids it. Periods past the end of the array are capped at 0 as well, so an empty array forbids selection in every period - give a positive value for each period the opportunity may be selected in. An entry below the matching time_period_minima is accepted and surfaces as a selection constraint conflict. Entries past selection_time_period_count are stored but not used.

selection_dependency.description: Selection dependencies: rules that change the select-ability of one (dependent) opportunity based on the selection of another (independent) one. This belongs to selection rules, and may vary per scenario.

items.description: One selection-dependency rule. Read as: for the dependent opportunity to be selected, the independent opportunity must/must-not be selected, within the range that timing (before/after/during) and timing_offset set relative to the dependent's selected period, in the given quantity ratio.

xid.description: The rule's identifier, assigned by the product, e.g. sd-271679; cannot be set or changed.

disabled.description: When true the rule is present but ignored. Optional; defaults to false.

dependent_opportunity.description: Name of the dependent opportunity — the one whose selection triggers the rule ("to select X…"). X is the dependent.

independent_opportunity.description: Name of the independent opportunity the dependent's selection depends on.

type.description: Whether the independent opportunity must, or must not, be selected. Allowed values: `Must` — The independent opportunity MUST be selected for the dependent to be selected.; `MustNot` — The independent opportunity MUST NOT be selected when the dependent is selected (an exclusive either/or condition). A MustNot rule carries no ratio: each_scale omitted, each_interest false, need_scale 1, need_interest false..

timing.description: Range direction of the timing relationship (over-all / before / after / during). Allowed values: `OverAll` — The relationship applies across all periods (no directional timing).; `Before` — The independent selection must occur at or before the dependent's period plus timing_offset.; `After` — The independent selection must occur at or after the dependent's period plus timing_offset.; `During` — The independent selection must occur exactly in the dependent's period plus timing_offset..

timing_offset.description: Signed number of periods that moves the boundary of the constrained range away from the dependent's selected period t: Before = independent at or before t + offset, After = independent at or after t + offset, During = independent exactly at t + offset. The sign does not encode direction (that is the timing field). Example: "B at least 8 periods after A" is dependent B, independent A, Must, Before, -8. After with +8 and the same roles is the reverse rule (A at least 8 periods after B).

each_scale.description: Ratio scale on the dependent side ('each' clause). With each_interest, expresses the dependent quantity in the 'N instances / R selections' ratio. Optional; unset means no limit on the dependent quantity (any number).

each_interest.description: When true the 'each' ratio is expressed in real-number selections (R, interest); when false it is expressed in instance counts (N).

need_scale.description: Ratio scale on the independent side ('need' clause), paired with need_interest.

need_interest.description: When true the 'need' ratio is expressed in real-number selections (R, interest); when false it is expressed in instance counts (N).

selection_group.description: Selection groups: containers that link the selection of opportunities (mutually inclusive or mutually exclusive), with group-level limits that override member constraints. This belongs to selection rules, and may vary per scenario.

groups.description: The selection groups and their members.

items.description: One selection group: a named set of member opportunities linked by the group type.

disabled.description: When true the group is present but its linking behaviour is ignored (members fall back to their individual constraints). Optional; defaults to false.

group_name.description: Unique name of the group. Referenced by group_limits.group_name.

type.description: Whether membership is mutually inclusive or mutually exclusive. Allowed values: `MutualInclusive` — Mutually inclusive: all members are selected if any member is selected, in the same period as the triggering member.; `MutualExclusive` — Mutually exclusive: only one member may be selected; the others are excluded and remain unavailable in later periods..

members.description: The member opportunities of this group.

items.description: One member of a selection group.

opportunity_name.description: Name of the member opportunity. Must match a defined opportunity.

disabled.description: When true this membership is removed from the group and the opportunity's own selection constraints re-apply. Optional; a new membership is enabled.

group_limits.description: Group-level selection limits, one per group, keyed by group_name. While a group's limits are active they take precedence over members' individual selection constraints.

items.description: Group-level selection limits applied to all members of one group. Inherits the same min/max/instance/per-period bounds as an opportunity limit; a group Max applies to each member (e.g. Max = 2 means each selected member may be selected up to twice), not to the count of members chosen.

group_name.description: Name of the group these limits apply to. Must match a group's group_name.

disabled.description: When true the constraint is present but ignored. Optional; defaults to false.

integer_only.description: When true the optimizer may only make whole (integer) selections of this unit — no partial/fractional selection.

interior_limit.description: Min Fraction: the minimum quantity that must be selected IF the unit is selected (it does not force selection). Applies per instance and only when non-integer selection is allowed; ignored when integer_only is true. Optional.

total_minimum.description: Minimum total selection summed across the entire span of eligible periods (aggregate, not per period). A positive value forces selection.

total_maximum.description: Maximum total selection summed across the entire span of eligible periods (aggregate, not per period). 0 forbids selection.

total_instances_minimum.description: Minimum number of instances (each in-period selection counts as one instance regardless of fractional size; 1.1 counts as two). A positive value forces selection. Optional.

total_instances_maximum.description: Maximum number of instances allowed. Optional.

time_period_minima.description: Per-period minimum selections, indexed by time period (element 0 = period 0). A positive entry forces selection in that period. May be empty (no per-period minima) or shorter than the horizon (unspecified periods are unbounded below). Entries past selection_time_period_count are stored but not used.

time_period_maxima.description: Per-period maximum selections, indexed by time period (element 0 = period 0). Caps selection in that period, and 0 forbids it. Periods past the end of the array are capped at 0 as well, so an empty array forbids selection in every period - give a positive value for each period the opportunity may be selected in. An entry below the matching time_period_minima is accepted and surfaces as a selection constraint conflict. Entries past selection_time_period_count are stored but not used.
